note: Civilizational core framing. Does not replace canonical definition in book_identity.json until Steve approves any amendment.

sacred_sentence.text: Power should always flow toward the people, never permanently away from them.

first_principle.text: The people are the nation's greatest source of productive capacity, creativity, innovation, and self-government.
first_principle.dignity_guardrail: A person is never merely a resource. People are citizens with inherent dignity and rights.

organizing_principle.text: Power should be distributed as close as possible to the people who create and sustain society.

subsidiarity.acknowledgement: Constitutional Capitalism shares the intuition of subsidiarity rather than presenting it as a brand-new discovery.
subsidiarity.working_statement: Authority, ownership, and economic benefit should remain as close as reasonably possible to the people and communities that create the value, unless a broader level of organization is demonstrably necessary.

power_hierarchy.name: Nation
power_hierarchy.emphasis: Essential for defense, interstate commerce, constitutional rights, monetary policy, and similar functions

power_movement_rule: Power moves upward only when the lower level cannot reasonably accomplish the task alone.

pillars.name: Stewardship
pillars.focus: Improve and pass on inheritance to the next generation

corporation_framing.primary_function: Produce goods and services efficiently and sustainably.
corporation_framing.working_statement: A corporation that benefits from a community shares responsibility for sustaining the conditions that allow that community to flourish.
corporation_framing.role: Constitutional partners in national prosperity — not enemies, not rulers, not governments.
corporation_framing.avoid: Wording that assigns corporations sole responsibility to feed or govern citizens.

community_economic_sovereignty.resilience_statement: Every community should possess enough productive capacity that it can remain resilient during national or global disruptions.

duty_of_improvement.statement: No generation inherits a perfect system. Every generation has a duty to improve it for the next.
duty_of_improvement.civic_virtue: Constructive improvement through evidence, reason, constitutional process, and respect for the rights of others.

civilizational_question: How should every institution of society work together to maximize human flourishing while preventing the concentration of unaccountable power?
ai_constitutional_question: Who owns the productivity of AI?

community_operating_system.role: Practical signature of the movement: playbooks and a Community Operating System architecture so the same principles adapt to different towns, counties, states, and nations.
community_operating_system.practical_question: Show me exactly how my town of 500 people becomes a town of 5,000 over the next 30 years.
community_operating_system.implementation_completeness_rule: No proposal is complete without an implementation pathway, measurable outcomes, estimated costs, anticipated tradeoffs, and evaluation/revision.
community_operating_system.note: Design agenda — Community OS is not an operating product; no invented town outcomes.

human_capital_doctrine.role: Pillar: deliberately build human capital infrastructure — multiple respected pathways of equal dignity; regional academies as pilot candidates, not locked statewide design.
human_capital_doctrine.first_principle: Every child should graduate with a meaningful pathway to productive adulthood through multiple respected pathways rather than a single model of success.
human_capital_doctrine.infrastructure_claim: A state should deliberately build human infrastructure with the same seriousness as physical infrastructure.
human_capital_doctrine.named_pilot_model: Arkansas regional civic and innovation academies (name undecided; design agenda)
human_capital_doctrine.note: Architecture and developing doctrine only — academies are pilot candidates; research precedes statewide statute.

essential_systems.role: Major system-design domain for banking, insurance, healthcare, pharmaceuticals, community health, and prevention — incentives and outcomes, not inherent-corruption conclusions.
essential_systems.constitutional_question: How should a society design essential systems so that private innovation and investment are rewarded while the public interest remains protected?
essential_systems.financial_principle: The financial system should primarily reward the creation of productive value rather than the extraction of value.
essential_systems.health_principle: A constitutional republic should measure success not only by how well it treats illness, but by how well it helps people remain healthy.
essential_systems.preventive_society_goal: Shift public investment gradually from paying for avoidable crises toward preventing those crises in the first place.
essential_systems.note: Architecture and developing doctrine only — Community Health Index is a design agenda; research precedes detailed sector legislation.

transparency_spine.role: Fourth institutional spine: public information held in trust — presumed open unless constitutionally or legally justified protections apply.
transparency_spine.guiding_principle: In a constitutional republic, government does not own public information. It holds public information in trust for the people, subject only to those limited protections necessary to preserve constitutional rights, legitimate privacy, public safety, and national security.
transparency_spine.openness_presumption: Government information created with public resources should be presumed open unless there is a constitutionally or legally justified reason to protect it. The burden should generally be on the government to explain why information is withheld.
transparency_spine.note: Architecture and developing doctrine only — People's Ledger is a design agenda; research precedes detailed open-records legislation.

public_service_spine.role: Defining institutional design doctrine: better outcomes with fewer layers, less friction, and greater accountability — not merely more or less government.
public_service_spine.defining_design_question: How do we build a government that delivers better outcomes with fewer layers, less friction, and greater accountability?
public_service_spine.foundational_principle: Government work should be among the highest forms of civic service. Public institutions should use technology to eliminate unnecessary administrative labor so human talent can be concentrated in judgment, problem-solving, public engagement, oversight, and service.
public_service_spine.friction_reduction_principle: Government should continuously reduce administrative friction while continuously improving public service.
public_service_spine.iconic_phrase: Government should become invisible—but never unaccountable.
public_service_spine.operational_rule: Use technology to remove unnecessary bureaucracy, use human talent where judgment and compassion matter, and keep every public institution visible to the people who own it.
public_service_spine.technology_doctrine: Automate the routine. Elevate the human.
public_service_spine.collect_once_principle: Collect once. Reuse securely with appropriate legal authorization.
public_service_spine.arkansas_objective: Build a state government that is small enough to understand, capable enough to serve, transparent enough to trust, and open enough for ordinary citizens to enter and improve.
public_service_spine.note: Architecture and developing doctrine only — Arkansas inventory/credential are design agendas; research precedes detailed administrative policy.

political_power_spine.role: Constitutional Capitalism cannot return economic power to the people while leaving political power concentrated in legislatures, parties, donors, governors, and courts.
political_power_spine.foundational_principle: No branch, party, officeholder, donor class, or temporary majority should be able to convert electoral victory into permanent control of the republic.
political_power_spine.trust_doctrine: Political authority is held in trust, never owned. Power must remain divided, visible, reviewable, locally rooted where possible, and continuously returnable to the people.
political_power_spine.anti_entrenchment: No temporary majority may use public power principally to make itself harder to remove, harder to investigate, or less accountable to the electorate.
political_power_spine.distributed_government_objective: Strong enough to protect rights and perform necessary public functions, but too divided, transparent, and accountable for any temporary faction to capture permanently.
political_power_spine.note: Second constitutional spine. Architecture and developing doctrine only — research precedes detailed political-structure policy.

family_spine.role: Major pillar: family-first republic — children as the greatest long-term asset, with inherent dignity independent of economic output.
family_spine.organizing_principle: A nation's greatest long-term asset is not its money, its corporations, or its natural resources. It is the children it raises.
family_spine.foundational_doctrine: Strong families create strong communities. Strong communities create a strong republic. Public institutions should strengthen families rather than replace them whenever possible.
family_spine.shared_responsibility_rule: Children are the shared responsibility of their families, their communities, and ultimately the constitutional republic until they are prepared to become healthy, capable, independent participants in society.
family_spine.note: Architecture only — reject 'productive' as a worth test; child-flourishing indicators null until sourced.

human_flourishing_benchmark.role: Defining benchmark: Did human life improve? Policy test: Does this measurably increase human flourishing?
human_flourishing_benchmark.note: Design agenda — 0/17 HFI domains sourced; architecture is not measurement; modeling remains 0%.

constitutional_citizenship_spine.role: Core doctrine: build civic capacity rather than merely expand rights — democracy as a skill learned through experience, preparation, viewpoint-neutral service, and meaningful youth contribution.
constitutional_citizenship_spine.foundational_doctrine: Self-government requires education. A constitutional republic has a duty to prepare every generation to understand its rights, its responsibilities, its institutions, and its ability to improve society through peaceful civic participation.
constitutional_citizenship_spine.central_question: How do we graduate every citizen prepared to participate responsibly in self-government?
constitutional_citizenship_spine.civic_merit_principle: Government should encourage participation, not ideology.
constitutional_citizenship_spine.viewpoint_neutrality_rule: Schools may recognize civic participation regardless of viewpoint, but may not require students to support or oppose any candidate, party, or policy position as a condition of graduation.
constitutional_citizenship_spine.voting_age_discipline: Do not simply declare voting begins at 16; explore preparation-conditioned local pilots with measurement before broader adoption.
constitutional_citizenship_spine.note: Architecture and developing doctrine only — Youth Councils, Civic Service Portfolio, Civic Achievement Transcript, and earlier local voting models are design/pilot agendas; civic credit must remain viewpoint-neutral; no invented civics-outcome statistics.

equal_standing_spine.role: Foundational constitutional principle: equal standing before the Constitution — equal protection and equal accountability without engineered equality of outcome.
equal_standing_spine.foundational_principle: Every person stands equal before the Constitution. Neither wealth, office, race, religion, political affiliation, social status, birthplace, celebrity, nor institutional influence shall increase or diminish the protection of the law or the accountability imposed by the law.
equal_standing_spine.blind_stage_principle: Justice should evaluate conduct before identity whenever constitutionally and practically possible.
equal_standing_spine.iconic_phrase: The Constitution should hear the evidence before it sees the person.
equal_standing_spine.closing_rule: No one is above the law. No one is beneath its protection.
equal_standing_spine.note: Architecture and developing doctrine only — complements Declaration On equality; does not rewrite the Declaration; no invented access-to-justice statistics.

justice_mechanism.role: Justice is the mechanism that determines whether liberty, ownership, opportunity, and accountability are real—or merely promised. Community safety is a complete system — prevent, protect, treat, secure, restore, return — not isolated police or prison reforms. Continuing extreme danger is answered by humane permanent incapacitation with continuing review — never by declaring people unworthy of reentry.
justice_mechanism.foundational_principle: Justice must protect the public, restrain wrongdoing, repair harm where possible, and return people to productive citizenship whenever safely achievable. It must never become a profit center, a political weapon, or a permanent system of social exclusion.
justice_mechanism.community_safety_doctrine: Public safety belongs to the community. Police exercise authority on the community’s behalf, courts administer justice in the public trust, and correctional institutions exist to protect society and prepare people for responsible return whenever return is safely possible. No public-safety institution should profit from human confinement.
justice_mechanism.central_promise: A just society protects people from harm without surrendering the humanity of those who have caused harm. It holds wrongdoing accountable, repairs what can be repaired, and never converts punishment into permanent power over a person’s life.
justice_mechanism.public_safety_promise: Every person should be protected from violence, exploitation, addiction, institutional abuse, and preventable disorder. Every victim should be supported. Every accused person should receive due process. Every dangerous person should be securely managed. Every person capable of restoration should receive a real path back. Every official exercising coercive authority should remain visible, reviewable, and accountable to the public.
justice_mechanism.permanent_public_safety_standard: No person loses human dignity, even when they lose liberty. Secure confinement may be necessary to protect society, but it must remain public, humane, productive, reviewable, and limited to the least restrictive conditions capable of maintaining safety.
justice_mechanism.note: Complete Community Safety and Restoration System architecture — not Declaration rewrite; Corps/Restoration Councils/Secure Public Safety Campuses are design agendas; research precedes detailed justice policy.

resource_sovereignty.role: Central doctrine: place-based resource rights, progressive pricing of extraordinary consumption, community return, restoration, and energy resilience — connecting stewardship, ownership, affordability, and corporate accountability.
resource_sovereignty.central_doctrine: Natural resources belong first to the place that bears the extraction, consumption, congestion, pollution, and long-term risk. Private enterprise may profit from using those resources, but the affected community must receive a direct, permanent, and measurable return.
resource_sovereignty.operational_rule: The greater the consumption, scarcity, risk, or damage, the greater the obligation to the affected community.
resource_sovereignty.governing_statement: Land, water, minerals, energy capacity, clean air, soil, infrastructure, and ecological resilience are part of a community’s inherited wealth. Those who consume them for private gain must pay their full public cost, restore what they damage, and return a fair share of the resulting prosperity to the people and place that made the activity possible.
resource_sovereignty.note: Architecture and developing doctrine only — Compacts, Ledger, and Exchange are design agendas; illustrative dividend percentages require modeling; research precedes detailed resource statutes.

community_food_security.role: Food as critical infrastructure and a strategic community asset — a broad Community Food Security System for testing models, not a single locked food-network structure.
community_food_security.central_principle: Every community should have the capacity to provide a meaningful share of its essential food needs while remaining connected to broader markets that increase resilience and economic opportunity.
community_food_security.rejected_principle: Mass production food becomes export only items.
community_food_security.governing_doctrine: Food is a strategic community asset. A prosperous constitutional republic strengthens local food production, supports efficient regional distribution, rewards stewardship of the land, reduces waste, and ensures that every community has reliable access to affordable, nutritious food while remaining connected to wider markets that provide resilience and economic opportunity.
community_food_security.note: Architecture and developing doctrine only — Network/Exchange/Dashboard/Reserves are design agendas; research precedes detailed food statutes.

promise_discipline: State principles, mechanisms, evidence, unknowns, success metrics, and correction paths — do not guarantee outcomes that cannot honestly be promised.

assistance_spine.role: Major pillar: assistance as human development — security without dependency traps; pathways to income, ownership, and participation.
assistance_spine.organizing_principle: No person should be abandoned when unable to meet essential needs. No institution should trap a capable person in dependency.
assistance_spine.foundational_doctrine: Guarantee security while dismantling dependency. Place every recipient on the correct pathway. Every additional hour of productive work should leave a household better off.
assistance_spine.ubi_posture: Reject universal basic income as the organizing alternative; advance Community Work Guarantee.
assistance_spine.note: Architecture — SNAP FY2024 scale sourced; phaseout rates and work-guarantee fiscal design require modeling/pilots; modeling remains 0%.

federalism_spine.role: Major pillar: limited, capable, transparent, focused federal government — not weak — under subsidiarity and constitutional-rights floors.
federalism_spine.organizing_principle: Power remains local unless its exercise requires national coordination, national uniformity, or protection of constitutional rights.
federalism_spine.central_statement: The federal government exists to protect constitutional liberty, defend the nation, preserve a fair national system, coordinate what communities and states cannot accomplish alone, and restrain powers that exceed local control. All other authority should remain as close to the people as competence and constitutional rights permit.
federalism_spine.note: Architecture only — no invented agency inventories or fiscal statistics; legal drafting remains 0%.
